transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Jordan (Hemisphere Head of AI), Priya (VP Eng), Marcus (Procurement), Elena (Cloud Ops)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call - Alex from Redwood, Samira our solutions engineer, Liam CSM. Jordan, Priya, Marcus, Elena from Hemisphere?
[00:07] Jordan: Yep, Jordan here. Hi all.
[00:10] Priya: Priya on my side.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:14] Elena: Elena, Cloud Ops.
[00:18] Alex: Great — purpose today is a renewal and expansion check-in, go over the Dedicated capacity upgrade you asked about, europe region expansion, and iron out next steps for contract extension. Want to hear any blockers first.
[00:28] Jordan: High level, we're happy with Redwood's latency at current hosted tier, but we've outgrown the open-hosted quota for a few high-throughput features. We're evaluating a Dedicated pool to get predictable throughput and lower unit cost. Also we need EU region for data residency for some pilot clinics.
[00:42] Samira: Thanks. From a SE perspective that's a common pattern — move high-throughput routes to Redwood Dedicated, keep lower-volume/experimental in hosted. We can propose a 3-tier capacity plan: small reserved pool for baseline, burst for spikes, and an optional reserved dedicated plus autoscale. I'll detail perf numbers in the deck.
[01:05] Priya: Curious on the autoscale — how quick is burst capacity? We have unpredictable spikes during morning triage.
[01:12] Samira: Current policy supports burst to shared capacity within seconds, but guaranteed throughput requires reserved capacity. Our autoscale can expand node count within 1-3 minutes depending on model and sequence lengths; for the EU region we can provision warm nodes to reduce cold start. There's some variance with quantized models vs FP16.
[01:34] Jordan: Cost question — what's the delta between reserved Dedicated and hosted for our workload? Last month we saw a huge increase during campaign X.
[01:41] Alex: We'll send a tailored pricing deck. Roughly, Dedicated reduces per-token compute costs by 20-40% at higher utilization and gives more predictable latency. We'll include modeled estimates using your sample QPS.
[01:55] Marcus: From procurement — we need contract extension timing. Our renewal window is end of June. We're looking at 12- or 24-month extension, possibly roll in dedicated capacity into the same contract. Also SOC 2 and KMS details are required for legal.
[02:10] Alex: Totally understood. Redwood's hosted and Dedicated both support SOC 2 compliance; we can share our attestation and security pack. For KMS we offer customer-managed keys integration via KMS/HSM in the Private deployment and also KMS options for Dedicated with customer key import. I'll attach the security docs.
[02:29] Elena: For the EU region we'll require VPC peering and specific subnets — do you have guidance on required network configs?
[02:36] Samira: Yes, we'll provide a VPC peering guide and the minimal set of CIDR/IP ranges and IAM roles. We'll also outline the VPC on-prem pattern if you decide to run Private in your own cloud.
[02:49] Jordan: On perf and quality — we want to validate the eu-west-1 latency and cost. Can SE run a benchmark with our workload?
[02:56] Samira: Absolutely. Proposed POC: 2-week technical POC in eu-west-1, run both your highest-throughput routes on a small dedicated pool, capture p50/p95/p99 and token costs, and test KV cache / prefix caching to show cost improvements. We'll produce a benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:14] Priya: What's needed from our side to start the POC?
[03:18] Samira: Sample prompt sets, expected QPS, a short list of models you want to test, and service accounts / IAM for the VPC. Also a contact for infra to set up peering.
[03:28] Jordan: I can share prompts and QPS by Tuesday.
[03:32] Alex: Great. Marcus, timeline for contracting?
[03:35] Marcus: We aim to finalize PO by mid-June if terms ok. Need an estimate and legal language by early next week ideally.
[03:43] Alex: We'll prioritize the pricing + contract terms and include a 12- and 24-month option with committed RU and overage rates. We'll also propose an SLA uplift for Dedicated — 99.9% with credits — is that what you're looking for?
[03:57] Priya: 99.9% sounds reasonable; we'll flag with legal if they want 99.95.
[04:02] Samira: Quick note on model variants and fallbacks — we can configure smart routing between lower-cost quantized variants and higher-quality variants when latency or capacity constraints occur. That helps cut unit-costs without full regression.
[04:16] Jordan: Good. Any concerns about model compatibility or prompt drift during migration?
[04:21] Samira: We'll run an eval set during POC to compare outputs between hosted and Dedicated model variants, track quality regressions and tie them to prompt sets so you can sign off.
[04:31] Elena: Security specifics — do you support SAML SSO and role-based RBAC on the console?
[04:36] Alex: Yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC scopes per-team. We'll share a short admin guide.
[04:44] Marcus: Contract question — are there any minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[04:48] Alex: We have flexible reserved tiers; for committed pricing there's a 3-month minimum for small pools and discounts on 12/24-months. We'll outline exact numbers in the deck.
[04:58] Jordan: For the EU pilot, we'd like a demo of cold-start behavior — how quickly KV cache warms. Can that be included?
[05:04] Samira: Yup — we'll instrument KV cache and prefix caching metrics, and include warm-node setups to show tail-latency improvements.
[05:12] Priya: Any required downtime for switchovers?
[05:15] Samira: None anticipated — traffic routing can be phased per-route with canary percentages. We can do blue/green style rollouts and automatic fallback policies so you never fully flip until you're ready.
[05:26] Jordan: Okay, recap me on what you said you'd send.
[05:29] Alex: We'll send: updated pricing deck with three capacity options and modeled cost using your sample QPS; security pack (SOC 2 attestation, KMS options, SAML config); POC runbook and schedule proposal for eu-west-1; and a draft contract with 12- and 24-month options and SLA uplift wording.
[05:45] Marcus: That works. If we get the deck Monday we can start legal review.
[05:49] Alex: We'll aim to get that by 2027-05-25.
[05:53] Jordan: For the POC start date, 2027-06-01 works for us.
[05:57] Samira: I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the POC runbook.
[06:00] Elena: I'll coordinate with infra; will send contact for peering.
[06:05] Alex: Anything else?
[06:07] Priya: One ask — include a cost sensitivity scenario where we show differences at 60%, 80%, 95% utilization. That helps our CFO.
[06:15] Alex: Will do.
[06:17] Liam (CSM): I'll make sure we have the success criteria documented and schedule a 1-week checkpoint during the POC.
[06:23] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:26] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the deck and docs.
